questions.q: In the capstone architecture, what does the language model do at the routing step?
options: It writes pandas code that the tool then executes
It returns a small JSON object saying which kind of question this is and which metric, grouping, and filters to use
It trains a new model on the sales table
It downloads the documents from the internet
questions.explain: The model only chooses from a menu of options in JSON. Your code validates that JSON and does the actual calculation.

questions.q: Why does the design forbid running code written by the model?
options: Because pandas cannot run generated code
Because it makes the tool slower
Because models cannot write Python
To keep numbers exact and avoid a whole class of security problems, since your own whitelisted code does the computing
questions.explain: Letting a model choose from a validated menu, and computing with your own code, is safer and more predictable than executing generated code.

questions.q: What should the tool do with "What is the airspeed of a swallow?"
options: Say it doesn't know, because retrieval scores fall below the threshold
Guess the most likely document and answer from it
Compute the average revenue instead
Crash and stop
questions.explain: A retrieval score threshold turns weak matches into an honest "I don't know" instead of an invented answer.

questions.q: Which parts of the capstone tool run for real in this course, and which are stubbed?
options: Everything is stubbed, including pandas
The language model runs for real; retrieval is stubbed
Retrieval, validation, and pandas run for real; the language model is a stub of hand-written rules
Nothing runs; the code is only shown
questions.explain: With no API key available, a rule-based fake stands in for the model. Everything else is real, and you should say so clearly in a portfolio write-up.

questions.q: Why write the test questions before building the tool?
options: The tool cannot start without them
They form an evaluation set with expected outcomes, so you can check the finished tool against a clear standard
They are required by the OpenAI API
They train the language model
questions.explain: Deciding what correct looks like up front gives you an evaluation set to run once the tool is built.
